focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Prompt: When you hear "thing(s)/something/stuff," pause and ask: What exact object, action, decision, pattern, or constraint do I mean?
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: I've done so many things, I've tried so many things, I've felt so many emotions and the biggest... -> I've tried many approaches and felt a wide range of emotions; the strongest was...

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Before you say “people” or “someone,” pause and ask: Who exactly is affected? Name that role.
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: Because I'm someone who's so purpose driven and I only wanna work on something that aligns... -> Because I'm a founder who's purpose driven and I only want to work on companies that align with my values...

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Micro-practice: Record a 60–90 second response to a prompt; play back and highlight every use of “really” or “very.” Replace each with one of the replacement options and re-record.
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: I have a very scary thought. -> I have a scary thought.

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: When you hear or plan to say 'way,' pause and ask: Do I mean method (approach), order (sequence), cause (mechanism), or indicator (signal)?
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: ...day and age sometimes is some people just are too afraid to embrace the way they think, and things they'd like to do. -> ...these days some people are too afraid to embrace how they think and what they'd like to do.

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Exercise: After a meeting, replace every “good/interesting/crazy” in your notes with one specific reason (impact, cause, or evidence).
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: Pretty good day. -> Day was productive: I finished two reports and cleared my inbox, which let me focus on planning tomorrow.

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Record a short spoken version of a note that begins with a hedge; time the first 5 seconds and count hedging phrases.
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: And so, yeah, I think they love me basically. -> And so, yeah, my view is they love me basically.

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Every time you say 'problem', ask whether it is a bottleneck, objection, failure mode, or proposal gap.
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: These abstract nouns stay one level above the actual failure mode, need, or proposal.

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Use 'pause' as today's forced replacement whenever you hear 'you know'.
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: Um, a small set of people were watching this line and saying, you know, "Th- this is gonna, this is gonna change a lot of things." One of those was Elon, who organized the meeting in, um, Puerto Rico in 2014. -> Um, a small set of people were watching this line and saying, "Th- this is gonna, this is gonna change a lot of things." One of those was Elon, who organized the meeting in, um, Puerto Rico in 2014.

focusTemplates.triggerQuestion: Use 'roughly' as today's forced replacement whenever you hear 'kind of / sort of'.
focusTemplates.exampleRewrite: Essentially, a lot of the problems that I'm dealing with are kind of fleeting and very context based. -> Essentially, a lot of the problems that I'm dealing with are roughly fleeting and very context based.

words.useWhen: A limit or condition shapes what is possible.
words.example: Energy is the real constraint, not motivation.

words.useWhen: Order matters and you need to name the order explicitly.
words.example: The morning sequence matters more than the task list.

words.useWhen: You need a word for the cue that starts a behavior.
words.example: The trigger should happen before the phone comes out.

words.useWhen: You are describing how much work moves through a system over time.
words.example: The workflow has low throughput because context switching is constant.

words.useWhen: A specific obstacle stops progress.
words.example: Clarity is the blocker, not effort.

words.useWhen: You mean the bar you expect yourself to meet.
words.example: The standard is clear; the execution is not.

words.useWhen: You are naming behavior that evades discomfort instead of solving it.
words.example: The rambling is a form of avoidance under pressure.

words.useWhen: You need a reference level for comparison.
words.example: Your baseline energy changes the way the transcript reads.

words.useWhen: You mean inner certainty or owned belief.
words.example: The sentence needs more conviction and less hedging.

words.useWhen: You are talking about the identity model you carry around yourself.
words.example: The self-concept behind the note sounds unstable.

words.useWhen: You mean a clear interpersonal limit.
words.example: The conversation needs a boundary, not more explanation.

words.useWhen: You are talking about restoring trust after friction.
words.example: The conflict needs repair before it needs analysis.

words.useWhen: The issue is mutual give-and-take.
words.example: The resentment comes from low reciprocity.

words.useWhen: You want to name the standard one side assumed.
words.example: The disappointment came from an unstated expectation.

words.useWhen: A relationship problem is driven by accumulated unresolved hurt.
words.example: The note sounds like resentment, not confusion.

words.useWhen: You mean the angle or interpretive lens that shapes how a point is received.
words.example: The framing made the answer sound defensive instead of decisive.

words.useWhen: You need a word for the main thread connecting your points.
words.example: The throughline disappears when the answer opens too many loops.

words.useWhen: You want to name a hedge or narrowing phrase precisely.
words.example: That qualifier weakens the opening sentence.

words.useWhen: You are describing pace and sentence rhythm in speech.
words.example: A steadier cadence would make the idea land harder.

words.useWhen: You want one word for verbal exactness and specificity.
words.example: The explanation needs more precision in the middle.
